summary: Sales manager Chris Klevan runs an impromptu one-to-one with closer Harry Edmonds, opening by apologising for how a preceding team sales meeting was handled and then coaching him through a personal crisis using a consciousness-map framework of pride, shame and courage. Harry says he is operating at roughly 20% of his sales ability, describes the closer his manager has seen as 'a shell of the closer who I am', and admits he no longer draws motivation from money — he stopped a sales training session that day because it 'just came from money'. Chris says what he saw on Harry's calls that day was 'avoidance and the passivity, which is pretty selfish', and puts a direct choice to him: either commit to holding prospects to a clear yes or no, or come off calls for a while. Harry answers 'I don't know', then says he would take time off if he could afford to, citing a 2k monthly payment he owes to Brian, and the call ends abruptly when his next prospect joins.
notable: The closer whose calls make up this entire batch was, on 27 May, in a documented performance dip his manager described as avoidance and passivity in objection handling — directly relevant to how this batch's close rate should be read.
Harry self-assesses as operating at ~20% of his current sales ability: 'the closer that is in front of you, that you have seen, is almost like... a shell of the closer who I am'.

Harry states his peak historical performance as 'when I'm at 100%, I'm closing at 40% on a bait-and-switch' — apparently referring to prior sales work, but a description a principal should be aware of.

Manager frames not handling an objection as a failure of moral courage, using a suicide analogy: 'If your mother came to you right now and was like, I'm going to kill myself, would you just be like, well, it's okay?'

Stated definition of the closer role: 'hold people to the highest standard of themselves... show them the truth at the end of the call of how they're showing up and how it's incongruent to who they want to be. And hold them to it and get them to a clear yes or no.'
Harry was untroubled by having closed nobody until it was raised in a team meeting: 'until that conversation on that team meeting, I was completely fine with the fact that I didn't close anybody'.
Leads move between closers informally and rooms cross over — Harry asks whether the 'Ram lead' was given to Andrew because 'his note-taker joined my room', and notes 'it's Kyla's lead anyway'.
Harry's stated financial pressure is the reason he keeps taking calls: 'If I had more money in my bank, I'd take the time off... I've got to pay Brian 2k at the end of the month'.
Call volume context: eight calls the previous week, five plus one more on this day.
Recording was disclosed at the top: 'This meeting is being recorded.'
